citations.quote: ## Study 1

phase.text: Not explicitly phased; long-term, multiple-dose, randomized multicenter study

citations.quote: The effect of Somatuline Depot on reducing GH and IGF-\beta-levels and control of symptoms in patients with acromegaly was studied in two long-term, multiple-dose, randomized multicenter studies.

design.text: One-year study with a 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled phase, a 16-week single-blind, fixed-dose phase, and a 32-week open-label dose-titration phase.

citations.quote: This one-year study included a 4-week double-blind, placebo-controlled phase, a 16-week single-blind, fixed-dose phase, and a 32-week open-label dose-titration phase.

population.text: Patients with active acromegaly based on biochemical tests and medical history; half (54/108) were somatostatin analog/dopamine agonist naive (or had stopped treatment for at least 3 months) and were required to have a mean GH level > 5 ng/mL at their first visit.

citations.quote: Patients with active acromegaly based on biochemical tests and medical history entered a 12-week washout period if there was previous treatment with a somatostatin analog or a dopaminergic agonist.

Half (54/108) of the patients had never been treated with a somatostatin analog or dopamine agonist, or had stopped treatment for at least 3 months prior to their participation in the study and were required to have a mean GH level > 5 \text{ ng}/\text{mL} at their first visit.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with a >50% reduction in mean GH from baseline to Week 4 after a single injection of drug or placebo.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with a >50% reduction in mean GH from baseline to Week 4 after a single injection of drug or placebo.

n.text: 108 patients enrolled in the initial placebo-controlled phase (51 males, 57 females); placebo N=25, lanreotide overall N=83.

citations.quote: A total of 108 patients (51 males, 57 females) were enrolled in the initial placebo-controlled phase of the study.

a total of 52 (63%) of the 83 lanreotide-treated patients had a > 50\% decrease in mean GH from baseline to Week 4 including 52%, 44%, and 90% of patients in the 60, 90 and 120 mg groups, respectively, compared to placebo (0%, 0/25).

result.text: In the double-blind phase, 52 (63%) of 83 lanreotide-treated patients had a >50% decrease in mean GH from baseline to Week 4 (52%, 44%, 90% in 60, 90, 120 mg groups) vs 0% (0/25) placebo. In the fixed-dose phase at Week 16, 72% of 107 lanreotide-treated patients had a >50% decrease.

citations.quote: a total of 52 (63%) of the 83 lanreotide-treated patients had a > 50\% decrease in mean GH from baseline to Week 4 including 52%, 44%, and 90% of patients in the 60, 90 and 120 mg groups, respectively, compared to placebo (0%, 0/25).

In the fixed-dose phase at Week 16, 72% of all 107 lanreotide-treated patients had a decrease from baseline in mean GH of > 50\% including 68% (23/34), 64% (23/36) and 84% (31/37) of patients in the 60, 90 and 120 mg lanreotide treatment groups, respectively.

citations.quote: ## Study 2
This was a 48-week, open-label, uncontrolled multicenter study which enrolled patients who had an IGF-1 concentration \ge 1.3 times the upper limit of the age-adjusted normal range.

design.text: Open-label, uncontrolled with a 4-month fixed-dose phase (four Somatuline Depot 90 mg injections at 4-week intervals) followed by a dose-titration phase.

citations.quote: Patients were initially enrolled in a 4-month fixed-dose phase where they received four deep subcutaneous injections of Somatuline Depot, 90 mg, at 4-week intervals.

population.text: Patients with an IGF-1 concentration ≥ 1.3 times the upper limit of the age-adjusted normal range.

citations.quote: This was a 48-week, open-label, uncontrolled multicenter study which enrolled patients who had an IGF-1 concentration \ge 1.3 times the upper limit of the age-adjusted normal range.

endpoint.text: Achievement of normal age-adjusted IGF-1 concentrations.

citations.quote: After 48 weeks of treatment with Somatuline Depot at 4-week intervals, 43% (27/63) of the acromegalic patients in this study achieved normal age-adjusted IGF-1 concentrations.

n.text: 63 patients (38 males, 25 females) entered the fixed-dose phase; 57 completed 48 weeks.

citations.quote: A total of 63 patients (38 males, 25 females) entered the fixed-dose phase of the trial and 57 patients completed 48-weeks of treatment.

result.text: After 48 weeks, 43% (27/63) of patients achieved normal age-adjusted IGF-1 concentrations; at the end of treatment, 24/63 (38%) had both normal IGF-1 and GH ≤ 2.5 ng/mL.

citations.quote: After 48 weeks of treatment with Somatuline Depot at 4-week intervals, 43% (27/63) of the acromegalic patients in this study achieved normal age-adjusted IGF-1 concentrations.

The proportion of patients with mean GH concentrations < 2.5 ng/mL increased significantly from 35% to 77% after the fixed-dose phase and 85% at the end of the study. At the end of treatment, 24/63 (38%) of patients had
both normal IGF-1 concentrations and a GH concentration of \le 2.5 ng/mL (see Table 4) and 17/63 patients (27%) had both normal IGF-1 concentrations and a GH concentration of <1 ng/mL.

indication.text: Somatuline Depot (lanreotide) Injection 60 mg, 90 mg and 120 mg is indicated for the long-term treatment of acromegalic patients who have had an inadequate response to surgery and/or radiotherapy, or for whom surgery and/or radiotherapy is not an option.

citations.quote: Somatuline Depot (lanreotide) Injection 60 mg, 90 mg and 120 mg is indicated for the long-term treatment of acromegalic patients who have had an inadequate response to surgery and/or radiotherapy, or for whom surgery and/or radiotherapy is not an option.

target_moa.text: Lanreotide is a somatostatin analog with high affinity for human somatostatin receptors (SSTR) 2 and 5; activity at SSTR 2 and 5 is the primary mechanism believed responsible for GH inhibition.

citations.quote: Somatuline Depot (lanreotide) Injection is a somatostatin analog indicated for:

Lanreotide has a high affinity for human somatostatin receptors (SSTR) 2 and 5 and a reduced binding affinity for human SSTR1, 3, and 4. Activity at human SSTR 2 and 5 is the primary mechanism believed responsible for GH inhibition.

Lanreotide has a high affinity for human somatostatin receptors (SSTR) 2 and 5 and a reduced binding affinity for human SSTR1, 3, and 4. Activity at human SSTR 2 and 5 is the primary mechanism believed responsible for GH inhibition. Like somatostatin, lanreotide is an inhibitor of various endocrine, neuroendocrine, exocrine and paracrine functions.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>5% in overall pooled data, N=416) were gastrointestinal disorders — diarrhea (37%), abdominal pain (19%), nausea (11%) — cholelithiasis and injection site reactions. Cholelithiasis and gallbladder sludge were reported in 20% of patients.

citations.quote: The most commonly reported adverse reactions reported by > 5% of patients who received Somatuline Depot (N=416) in the overall pooled safety studies in acromegaly patients were gastrointestinal disorders (diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, constipation, flatulence, vomiting, loose stools), cholelithiasis and injection site reactions.
Diarrhea	81	48	155	37

In clinical studies involving 416 acromegalic patients treated with Somatuline Depot, cholelithiasis and gallbladder sludge were reported in 20% of the patients.
